# Naming the fund-unit split of a bill's transaction as the settlement.
#
# The bill side of the units refusal. A bill's settlement is a *positive*
# figure on the payable — the posting's sign reversed — and +1.000 is
# positive, so the sign guard has nothing to say. The commodity is what
# refuses it.
#
# It is also what the message has to get right: a bill has a payable, not a
# receivable, and telling a reader their split cannot be moved "onto the
# receivable" names an account their book has not got.
#
# What this fixture produces: a refusal naming the account and the payable,
# with the units still on the fund.
#
# Verified by
# tests/integration/test_linking_a_split_not_on_the_receivable.py.
bill "BILL-USD-001"
  vendor_id: "V-US"
  currency: USD
  date_opened: 2026-01-05
  entry:
    date: 2026-01-05
    description: "Parts"
    account: "Expenses:Supplies"
    quantity: 1
    price: 100
    taxable: false
  posted:
    date: 2026-01-05
    due: 2026-02-05
    ap_account: "Liabilities:Accounts Payable USD"
    memo: "Bill BILL-USD-001"
    accumulate: true
  payment:
    date: 2026-03-22
    amount: 100
    account: "Assets:Bank:USD"
    txn_guid: "1f2a3b4c5d6e7f8a9b0c5f6a7b8c9d0e"
    txn_split_guid: "3b4c5d6e7f8a9b0c5f6a7b8c9d0e1f2a"
